provenance.notes: Leaned on how patients choose a specialist at a large centre: doctor first, then insurance network, language and clinic days. Licence numbers are placeholders. Unsure on the insurer pre-approval tracker and patient app ranges; they swing with the clinic system's integration options.

pageStructurePlus.section: Doctor directory with specialty and language filters
pageStructurePlus.contains: Every doctor at the polyclinic with photo slot, specialty, languages spoken, gender, clinic days and a book-with-this-doctor button, filterable on a phone
pageStructurePlus.why: At a multi-specialty centre, patients choose the doctor first and the building second. Filters by language and gender matter to many families.

pageStructurePlus.section: A page for each specialty department
pageStructurePlus.contains: Per department: what kinds of visits it handles in general terms, its doctors, clinic days, equipment on site, insurance accepted and booking for that specialty only
pageStructurePlus.why: Someone searching for a paediatrician or a dermatologist needs that department's page, not the medical centre's home page. Each one also ranks on its own.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Each package with the tests included listed plainly, who it is designed for, preparation notes, [price] placeholders and online booking, with no claims about what it will find
pageStructurePlus.why: Packages are planned purchases, often for a parent or a whole family. A clear list of what's included is what turns a browser into a booking.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The insurance networks the centre belongs to as a list the billing team confirms, how direct billing works, what needs pre-approval and how long approval usually takes in plain words
pageStructurePlus.why: Network membership decides which polyclinic many patients can use at all. Answering it on the page saves reception a call per patient.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Per doctor: qualifications, where trained, years in practice, languages and [licence number] as placeholders the medical director verifies before publishing
pageStructurePlus.why: Patients check a specialist's background before booking, and in some places the regulator expects licence details shown with the doctor's name.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Employer health check and clinic-access packages, family bundles, how an HR manager requests a proposal, and a contact for the corporate desk
pageStructurePlus.why: Employers and large families buy once for many people. A dedicated page puts the multi-specialty centre on the shortlist.

designDirections.name: Specialty Finder
designDirections.bestFor: Centres with several specialties that need one clean way to pick a department and request a visit
designDirections.headlineSample: Every specialty under one roof in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a neutral grotesque keep a long list of departments readable. The hero is a grid of specialty cards, so the visitor's first tap is the department they need.

designDirections.name: Doctor First
designDirections.bestFor: Established polyclinics booking by doctor, specialty and insurance network, with a full doctor directory
designDirections.headlineSample: Book a {City} specialist by name, language or day
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's Private Vault combo. A warm cream ground and a refined serif feel like a private clinic, which suits families choosing a specialist they'll see for years.

designDirections.name: Medical Centre Flagship
designDirections.bestFor: Large multi-specialty centres with health check packages, corporate plans and patients who compare on reputation
designDirections.headlineSample: A {City} medical centre families trust for every specialty
designDirections.whyItFits: Navy with brass accents and an editorial serif carry a flagship feel without looking cold. It suits a centre selling packages and corporate plans alongside visits.

openers.line: Your medical centre lists many specialties on the home page, but each one leads to the same contact form. A parent looking for a paediatrician wants that department's doctors and clinic days.
openers.hook: Click three specialties on their site. If they all end at one general form, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A page and booking for each specialty department: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find a list of your doctors with their specialty, languages and clinic days. At a polyclinic, most patients choose the doctor first and the centre second.
openers.hook: Look for a doctors or team page. Note whether it shows specialty, languages and days.
openers.linkLine: A doctor directory with specialty and language filters: {demo-link}

openers.line: Booking at your polyclinic is a form that says someone will call back. A patient who wants an evening dermatology slot would rather pick the time than wait by the phone.
openers.hook: Try the booking path on their site. Note whether it ends at a request or a real time slot.
openers.linkLine: Booking by specialty, doctor and time: {demo-link}

openers.line: People keep asking in your comments whether the medical centre is in their insurance network. A page listing networks and direct billing would take those calls off reception.
openers.hook: Scroll their comments and reviews for insurance or network questions. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: Insurance networks and direct billing on one clinic page: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Health check packages in a PDF
openers.line: Your health check packages live in a PDF on social media. A package page with what's included, preparation notes and booking would sell them every week, not just after a post.
openers.hook: Find their latest package post. Note whether the site has the same packages with booking.
openers.linkLine: Health check packages people can book at the medical centre: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your doctor profiles show a name and specialty but no qualifications, languages or licence details. Someone choosing a specialist at a medical centre checks those before booking.
openers.hook: Open two doctor profiles. Note what's missing; never quote a licence number you didn't see.

openers.line: Your posts are written in two languages, but the polyclinic website is in one. Families choose a medical centre where they can read every page, including the doctor profiles.
openers.hook: Only if they post in more than one language. Note which language the site lacks.

openers.line: Saw a new specialist joined the centre recently. A profile with their clinic days and booking would fill their first weeks faster than a single announcement post.
openers.hook: Only if they announced a new doctor. Note the name and specialty from the post.
openers.linkLine: A specialist profile ready to take bookings: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your medical centre site was slow on my phone and the specialties menu hid behind a second menu. Most patients look for a specialist on their phone between other things.
openers.hook: Load it on mobile data and count the taps to book any specialty. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The polyclinic site rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing mentions corporate health plans, but there's no page where an HR manager can see the options or request a proposal from the medical centre.
openers.hook: Check the listing and site for corporate or employer wording. Note whether there's a contact for it.
openers.linkLine: A corporate health plan page for the centre: {demo-link}

openers.line: Many of your reviews thank a specific doctor by name. Those public comments belong on that doctor's profile, where a patient comparing specialists will read them.
openers.hook: Read recent reviews and list which doctors are named most. Quote the warmest one.
openers.linkLine: Doctor profiles with their public reviews: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your centre has its own lab and pharmacy, which saves patients a second trip after a specialist visit. The site barely mentions either.
openers.hook: Check their listing photos or posts for an on-site lab or pharmacy. Note whether the site mentions them.
openers.linkLine: Lab and pharmacy shown on the medical centre site: {demo-link}

openers.line: Several of your specialties run evening or weekend clinics, but the site doesn't say which. Working patients choose the polyclinic that fits after office hours.
openers.hook: Find any post or listing note about late or weekend clinics. Note which departments.
openers.linkLine: Clinic days and evening hours by specialty: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw your centre is recruiting doctors and nurses. Clinicians who might relocate for a role study a medical centre's site and doctor profiles before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted vacancies recently. Note the roles and specialties.
openers.linkLine: A careers page for the multi-specialty centre: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} post from your centre explained a specialty's service clearly without overselling it. It deserves to live on that department's page.
openers.hook: Pick their newest awareness-day or department post and name it exactly. Never reference a patient.
openers.linkLine: That department's page with your post on it: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, I was looking at medical centres in {City} and noticed {Business Name} has many specialties, but no doctor directory and no way to book a specific department online.

I build sites for polyclinics: a doctor directory with language and specialty filters, a page per department, booking by doctor and an insurance network page. I've sketched a sample for your centre, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Shall I send it? And is it best with you, or with your general manager or marketing lead?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up on my note about {Business Name}. Here's the sample: {demo-link}

It has a doctor directory, a page for each specialty, booking by doctor and time, health check packages, an insurance network page and a corporate plans page. Doctor licence details are placeholders for your medical director to verify. Nothing goes live without your approval.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for multi-specialty medical centres here in {City}. I sent a note a few days ago about {Business Name}, did it reach you?"

IF RECEPTION ANSWERS:
"Thank you. Who looks after the website and marketing for the centre? I'd like to send them a sample."

IF NO:
"Short version: I built a sample site with a doctor directory, a page for each department, booking by doctor and an insurance page, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email it to you and your medical director?"

IF YES:
"What did you and the medical director think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"It connects to the clinic system you already run, so doctors' real clinic days show on the site. The build runs {Build Range} depending on specialties, languages and integrations, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, new doctor profiles and updates. For a centre your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, phased by department."
"Could we take twenty minutes with you, the medical director and whoever handles insurance?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a phased scope you can share. Doctors' details are verified by your medical director before anything publishes."

objections.objection: Every doctor will want their profile written differently.
objections.handler: "They can. Each profile follows one structure, the doctor edits their own paragraph, and the medical director verifies qualifications. I chase the doctors so your team doesn't."

objections.objection: Our clinic system's booking is clunky; we'd rather take calls.
objections.handler: "Then the site books into the slots you choose to release, and everything else still comes to reception. Patients who want to pick a time can; the rest still call."

objections.objection: The regulator has to approve our advertising.
objections.handler: "Understood. Package and specialty pages are written without claims and organised so your team can submit them for approval where that's required. Nothing promotional goes live first."

objections.objection: We already have a site from the group's IT team.
objections.handler: "Fine, then let's see if it answers what patients ask: which doctor, which language, which insurance, which day. If it does, keep it. If not, I can build into it or replace it."

objections.objection: We'd need it in two languages.
objections.handler: "Planned from the start. Both languages share one structure, and a fluent staff member checks the translation before every page publishes."

objections.objection: It's a big decision for the partners.
objections.handler: "It should be. I'll send a one-page phased scope; phase one is the directory and two departments, so the partners see it working before committing to the rest."
"{Build Range} depending on specialties, languages and integrations. For your centre about {Build Price}, plus {Care Range} a month for hosting, new doctor profiles and updates."

email.subject: Doctor directory and booking for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for medical centres in {City}, and I made a sample for {Business Name} with a doctor directory and booking for each specialty. I'll email the link so you can share it with the medical director. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking down the doctor directory sample I built for {Business Name} on Friday.

Should I keep it up for the partners to look at? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, centres often add a specialty or a few doctors at the start of a new year, and you came to mind.

The sample with the doctor directory and department booking is still here for {Business Name}, same scope and price. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Price by department and doctor count; a polyclinic with many specialties is many small sites sharing one booking engine.
Quote the clinic-system connection after a technical call; showing real clinic days is the hardest and most valuable part.
Charge for the second language as its own phase, with a fluent reviewer named in the scope.
Doctor profiles are cheap to build and slow to approve; price the chasing and verification, not the page.
Health check packages and corporate plans each need the medical director's sign-off and, in some places, regulator approval.
Never write diagnostic or outcome claims; testimonials and patient photos only with written consent on file.

lineItems.description: Max with verified qualifications, languages, clinic days, public reviews and a booking link straight to that doctor.
Max with its own doctors, equipment notes, insurance list, preparation guidance and specialty-only booking.

lineItems.item: Clinic-system booking by doctor and specialty
lineItems.description: Max when real slots come from every doctor's schedule with visit types, insurance rules and deposits.

lineItems.item: Health check package pages with booking
lineItems.description: Max with several packages, add-on tests, preparation notes and booking tied to lab availability.
Max when every doctor profile and department page is translated, right-to-left layout is needed, and fluent staff review all of it.

lineItems.item: Insurance network and direct billing page
lineItems.description: Max when networks differ by department and the pre-approval process is explained step by step.
Max with headcount, package choice, billing details and routing to the corporate desk.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profiles for the centre and each doctor
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Patients search a specialist's own name as often as the medical centre's. I keep the centre's profile and each doctor's listing accurate, with clinic days and a booking link."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once doctor profiles are live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Doctor portrait sessions
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One day of consistent portraits for every doctor and a few department shots, so the directory looks like one polyclinic, not a collage of passport photos."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or when several new doctors join.

whatElseYouSell.name: Promotion approval file for packages and specialties
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Health check offers and specialty promotions often need regulator sign-off in some countries. I write the polyclinic copy without claims and assemble the file your team submits."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, before any package promotion runs.

whatElseYouSell.name: Secure enquiry and booking forms with compliant hosting
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Department enquiries and doctor bookings carry health details. Forms ask only for what booking needs, sit on hosting set up for medical data, and your privacy officer gets the paperwork."

whatElseYouSell.name: Testimonial, consent and patient-photo policy
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short policy every department follows: no patient story or photo without signed consent, how consent is stored, and how a patient withdraws it. The multi-specialty centre speaks with one voice."

whatElseYouSell.name: Accessibility audit in both site languages
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Older patients and people with disabilities use a polyclinic more than most sites. I audit the directory and booking in each language, fix the failures and publish an access statement."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, after the second language launches.

whatElseYouSell.name: Health awareness calendar campaigns
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Awareness days give each department a reason to post. I plan the calendar, write general-information posts the specialists approve, and link each one to that department's booking."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review invitations by doctor
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Patients are invited to review the specialist they saw, not just the building, with wording the medical director approves. Doctors' profiles fill with real, public comments."

whatElseYouSell.name: Corporate plan sales sheet and landing page
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page sheet and a landing page for HR managers showing the centre's specialties, packages and direct billing, so the corporate desk has something to send after every call."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, with the corporate plans page.

withoutAI.route: Home nursing providers the centre refers to
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When your doctors arrange nursing at home after a clinic visit, families look up the provider. Those companies need a clear service and booking site, and your introduction helps."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Home nursing providers depend on clinic referrals and take a referring centre's suggestion seriously.

withoutAI.route: Medical supply and mobility shops nearby
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Patients leave your specialists with a list of braces, monitors or mobility aids. The medical supply shop down the road needs a catalogue with click-and-collect."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply shops live on clinic foot traffic and value the centre's goodwill.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Some of your visiting consultants also run a practice elsewhere. Once they've seen their profile on your polyclinic site, they'll want the same for their own clinic."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Doctors who like their profile are the easiest introduction there is.

withoutAI.route: Insurance brokers selling corporate health plans
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The brokers who place employers into your network need a plain site explaining plans and networks. Your corporate desk works with them weekly."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Brokers and the corporate desk send each other business and trust each other's recommendations.

withoutAI.route: Physiotherapy centres that take post-specialist referrals
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When your orthopaedic doctors refer patients for physio outside the centre, that clinic's booking page is the next step. A word from you opens the conversation."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Physio centres compete for specialist referrals and listen to the source.

withoutAI.route: Patient escort and medical translation services
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Patients travelling in for treatment use escort and translation services your centre already knows. They need a site that explains services and takes bookings in several languages."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: These firms get their clients through clinics and value any introduction from one.

withAI.route: Visit scheduling assistant for home nursing providers
withAI.pitchLine: "Families request home nursing visits by message; an assistant offers times that fit the nurses' rota and confirms them, passing anything clinical to a coordinator."
withAI.whyItWorks: Coordinators spend hours on scheduling messages, and faster replies win the family.

withAI.route: Order and stock assistant for medical supply shops
withAI.pitchLine: "Patients leaving the medical centre ask whether a brace or monitor is in stock and in which size. An assistant answers from the shop's own stock list and holds the item for collection."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small shops can't answer the phone all day, and each held item is a sale.

withAI.route: Plan comparison assistant for insurance brokers
withAI.pitchLine: "Employers ask brokers which clinics are in which plan. An assistant answers from the broker's own network lists and books a call for anything about cover."
withAI.whyItWorks: Brokers sell on responsiveness, and network questions are repetitive.

withAI.route: Home exercise reminders for physiotherapy centres
withAI.pitchLine: "Patients get reminders of the exercises their physiotherapist set, worded from the therapist's own notes and approved by them, with a link to book the next session."
withAI.whyItWorks: Physio centres want patients to come back for the full course, and the reminders bring them.

withAI.route: Booking and profile assistant for visiting specialists
withAI.pitchLine: "Patients message the specialist's private practice about fees, location and availability, and an assistant answers from the practice's own details and books a slot."
withAI.whyItWorks: Solo specialists have thin front desks, and quick replies fill their clinic days.

withAI.route: Travel and document checklist assistant for escort services
withAI.pitchLine: "Travelling patients get a checklist of documents, appointment times and pickup details in their language, drafted by an assistant and checked by the coordinator."
withAI.whyItWorks: Coordinators juggle many patients, and fewer missed documents mean fewer missed appointments.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call callback queue by department
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Unanswered calls are logged by the specialty the caller chose, texted a booking link for that department, and placed on reception's callback list in order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their phone menu options and wording the medical director approves.

softwareAI.name: Doctor-by-doctor review response suggestions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a review names one of your doctors, the patient relations team gets a suggested reply in the polyclinic's tone that thanks them without confirming any visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs approved reply examples and privacy rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Package booking confirmations with preparation notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Anyone booking a health check package gets a confirmation with fasting and preparation notes for that package and a reminder the evening before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs preparation notes per package approved by the lab and medical director.

softwareAI.name: Live clinic days from the scheduling system
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each doctor's real clinic days and next free slot show on their profile, pulled from the centre's schedule, so the directory is never out of date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs integration access to their clinic system and a list of visit types.

softwareAI.name: Health check package checkout
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Patients choose a health check package, add tests, pick a date and pay online, and the lab sees the booking with everything they need."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs package prices, add-on rules and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Department finder assistant on the site
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A patient types what they need in plain words and the assistant suggests which polyclinic department books that kind of visit. It never diagnoses and sends urgent symptoms to emergency services."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs department descriptions, approved routing rules and the medical director's sign-off. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Insurance pre-approval tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every procedure waiting on insurer approval sits on one board with its status and date, so the billing team chases the right ones and patients get told quickly."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their approval workflow and the insurers they deal with most.

softwareAI.name: Pre-approval request drafts for doctor review
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The billing team gets a draft pre-approval request from the doctor's note in each insurer's format, which the doctor checks before it is submitted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, with the tracker. Needs insurer templates and privacy review. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; doctors approve every request.

softwareAI.name: Corporate client portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Employers book health checks for staff, track who has attended and download invoices, without emailing the polyclinic's corporate desk."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs corporate package rules, consent wording and billing setup.

softwareAI.name: Bilingual page drafts with medical review
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New department pages and doctor profiles are drafted in the second language and queued for a fluent clinician to check, so both versions of the medical centre site stay in step."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the second language launches. Needs a named reviewer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Recruitment pipeline for doctors and nurses
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for every specialty land on one board with their licence status, interview stage and start date, shared by the medical director and HR."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their hiring steps and who approves each role.

softwareAI.name: Licence and credential renewal reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each doctor and nurse gets reminders before a licence or certificate expires, and HR sees who is overdue, so no one at the clinic practises on a lapsed licence."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, with the pipeline. Needs current expiry dates for every clinician.

softwareAI.name: Clinician applicant summaries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For each doctor or nurse applicant, the medical director gets a one-page summary of training, licences and specialty experience drawn from the CV, with gaps flagged."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs must-haves per specialty. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Reception call summaries by department
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Calls to reception, recorded with consent, become a short summary filed to the right department with a task, so a patient's question reaches the specialist's team."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs call recording with consent notices and phone system access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Internal referral routing between departments
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When one specialist refers a patient to another department, the referral and a booking request reach that team at once, and the patient gets a time before they leave."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs their referral rules and clinic system access.

softwareAI.name: Lab result cover note drafts for doctor sign-off
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A plain-language cover note for routine lab results is drafted for the doctor to edit and approve before the patient sees anything. The doctor's words, faster."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs result formats, note templates and a privacy review. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; doctors approve every note.

softwareAI.name: Follow-up appointment nudges after a specialist visit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Patients whose specialist asked to see them again get a message with that doctor's next free slots, so follow-ups don't drift to another clinic."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a follow-up flag in their clinic system and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Department performance dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Bookings, empty slots, no-shows and new patients by specialty and doctor on one screen, so the general manager sees which departments need marketing and which need doctors."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs three months of booking data by department.

softwareAI.name: Consultation note drafts from doctor dictation
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Specialists talk through the consultation and a note is drafted in their department's template, ready for them to correct and sign before it is saved."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 10. Needs templates per specialty, patient consent wording and privacy review. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Patient app with results, bookings and family profiles
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Patients book any doctor, see reviewed results, pay and manage their children's and parents' appointments in the medical centre's own app."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 12. Needs deep clinic-system integration, payments and a full privacy review.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the doctor directory for other medical centres
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The doctor directory, department pages and booking I built for one polyclinic suit any multi-specialty centre, loaded with their own doctors."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first centre paid for the schedule integration; the next ones need only content.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The hospital group's marketing or digital team
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your outpatient clinics are buried in the hospital site. A dedicated directory and department booking for them is a contained project with clear results."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Hospitals buy in large, central projects, and outpatient booking is a visible gap.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You send travelling patients to partner centres. A partner page per centre with doctors and packages, in your clients' languages, makes your offer clearer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Facilitators sell on clarity and trust, and the directory content already exists.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The health insurer's provider relations team
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your network clinics describe themselves badly. Offer them a standard page kit with directory, networks and direct billing explained the same way."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Insurers want members to find network providers easily, and a kit scales across their list.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency handles ads for medical centres but can't build schedule-driven directories. I deliver it under your name."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the account and need the integration skills they don't have.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each centre you acquire comes with its own site. One directory and booking platform across the group makes every acquisition look like part of a whole."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Investors want acquisitions unified quickly, and a repeatable platform fits that plan.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The association, as a member benefit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member clinics a site template with doctor credential display, privacy-safe forms and approval-ready copy already built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want concrete member benefits, and compliance is the question members keep asking.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Day-surgery centres need the same surgeon directory, procedure pages and insurer approval tracking I built for a polyclinic."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Similar buyers with the same parts, so most of the build carries over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Wellness companies sell health checks to employers and need clinics to deliver them. The corporate portal I built can carry their programmes across several centres."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: They already buy employer-facing software and need partner clinics wired in.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Bilingual clinic template for other cities
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The two-language structure, translated policies and doctor profiles I built suit any multi-specialty centre serving families in two languages."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Translation and layout work is done once; each new centre needs its own content only.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one multi-specialty centre per district. The centres competing with you in {City} won't get the same directory from me."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Centres value not sharing a builder with their nearest rival, and the structure carries over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Finishing stalled directory and booking projects
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The centre with a half-built site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your new site stalled at the doctor profiles or the booking connection. I can finish it on a structure already running at another medical centre."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: They've already decided and budgeted; they need someone to finish the hard part.

upsellLadder.offer: Medical centre site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: The general manager and medical director approve phase one: directory and first departments.
upsellLadder.line: "Build and care plan together means a new doctor's profile or a changed clinic day is updated within the week, without a new quote."

upsellLadder.offer: Google profiles for the centre and each doctor
upsellLadder.trigger: Bookings start arriving through doctor profiles, and patients still find old listings by searching a doctor's name.
upsellLadder.line: "Patients are searching your doctors by name. Their listings should send them straight to the right profile."

upsellLadder.trigger: Package pages get visits, and reception is booking them by phone.
upsellLadder.line: "People are reading the health check packages. Let them choose, add tests and pay without calling."
